key_insight: This paper moves beyond single-point verification by introducing symbolic properties for DRL agents, enabling sound reasoning about agent behavior over ranges of system states rather than isolated inputs.
problem_solved: Existing verification approaches in systems and networking check properties only at fixed input points, offering limited coverage and weak guarantees; the paper addresses the need to verify safety, performance, and robustness of DRL agents across continuous state regions encountered in practice.
method: Introduce a compact symbolic property language to express relations and constraints over sets of inputs and expected outputs (e.g., monotonicity, bounds, invariants).
Translate trained DRL policies into a symbolic/set-based representation (using piecewise-linear abstractions, bounding techniques, or constraint encodings) suitable for automated analysis.

Apply reachability/constraint solving to check symbolic properties over state regions and evaluate the approach on representative systems and networking benchmarks (e.g., congestion control, resource allocation, adaptive streaming).
impact: Provides practitioners with scalable, higher-coverage tools to certify safety and performance of DRL agents in real-world systems and networks, reducing surprising failures and guiding safer deployment and debugging.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: policy -> symbolic abstraction -> property checker -> verdict (safe/violated)
State-space heatmap: regions colored by property satisfaction vs. violation to illustrate coverage improvements over point checks
Use-case icons: small network, video streaming, wireless resource blocks linking to example property checks
Before/after bar chart: number of discovered violations and coverage comparing point-based vs. symbolic-property analysis
paper_title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
paper_authors: Mohammad Zangooei, Jannis Weil, Amr Rizk, Mina Tahmasbi Arashloo, Raouf Boutaba
